plain: To meddle in matters that are not your concern.

webster.text: To meddle in the affairs of others, in which one has no concern; to meddle officiously; to interpose or interfere improperly.

example.quote: Two causes prevail to make them intermeddle in such cases: — one is, to preserve the balance of power ; the other, to preserve their trade.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 18, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
